Title: Битва за Донбасс: главное 31 октября

Summary: 
According to Ukrainian intelligence, Russian President Vladimir Putin set two deadlines for Russia's military to capture the entire Donetsk Oblast: initially by autumn 2022, then by March 1, 2023, neither of which was met. From July 2022, after the capture of Lysychansk (completing the occupation of Luhansk Oblast), to autumn 2022, Russian forces made minimal territorial gains. In September 2022, Ukrainian counteroffensive operations led to the loss of significant Russian-held territory in Donetsk and Kharkiv Oblasts, and minor gains in Luhansk. In January 2023, Russia captured the small town of Siversk (Solodar), and by May had secured most of Bakhmut, where the UK Ministry of Defence reported Russian forces lost one soldier per 48 centimeters of territory. From May 2023, Ukrainian forces conducted offensive operations in the Bakhmut direction and, from June 2023, broke through the southern front at the border of Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia Oblasts. However, by October 2023, Russia resumed offensive operations, losing Avdiivka by the end of February 2024 and Ugledar in early October. As of October 31, 2024, Russian forces are pressing on multiple fronts in the east: Pokrovsk, Kupiansk-Limansk, and Bakhmut. The Kremlin continues its aim to seize all of Donetsk Oblast. Frontline positions as of October 31 include: Severodonez'k, Chasiv Yar, Kostiantynivka, with fighting near Shcherbinivka and Petrivka to the south, and Yablunivka and Rusyn Yar to the west. In the Pokrovsk direction, Russian forces are advancing in the city and its southern flank (Zvirovo, Kotlyno, Chunyshino), with gains in Pokrovsk itself, and attempts to expand a salient between Mirnograd, Drobopillya, and Kostiantynivka (Rodynske, Shakhovo, Novoekonomichne, Zapovidne, Novotoretske). To the west of Pokrovsk, attacks are advancing toward Dnipro Oblast (Molodetske, Udaчne, Novonikolaivka, with progress near the latter). In the tri-border area of Donetsk, Dnipro, and Zaporizhzhia Oblasts, attacks into Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia are possible after Russian advances near Velyka Novosilka. On the Luhansk front, Ukrainian forces have liberated several villages, including Kar'mazynivka, Myasozharivka, and Nevske, and earlier 6 settlements on the border with Kharkiv Oblast: Novolubivka, Hrekovka, Novoehorovka, Andriivka, Stelmakhivka, and Nadiya. On September 20, 2023, the General Staff confirmed Ukrainian operations in Luhansk Oblast, including strikes on Russian troop concentrations near Novoaidar and Svatoe. The timeline of the occupation of Luhansk Oblast prior to Ukraine’s counteroffensive includes: Lysychansk, Severodonez'k, Zolotye-Gorsk, Kremenna, Rubizhne, Popasna, Starobils'k, Belokurikino, Novopskov, Belovodsk, Melove, and Markivka. On September 21, 2023, 215 Ukrainian soldiers were released from Russian captivity, including 108 from the 'Azov' Battalion. The exchange involved 200 prisoners for Viktor Medvedchuk, a Russian-linked Ukrainian politician, and 15 for 55 Russian prisoners. Five Ukrainian commanders were extracted to Turkey under President Erdogan’s personal protection. On October 17, 37 women from Azovstal were returned home, bringing the total number of released female soldiers and civilians to 108. On July 29, Russia claimed that Ukrainian forces killed 53 Azovstal prisoners in a HIMARS strike on a camp in Olenivka. Ukraine denies this and calls it a massacre; experts from the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) found the damage inconsistent with a HIMARS strike, noting extensive internal fire damage instead. Radio Donbass Realii analyzed local Telegram and VK groups near Olenivka and found no evidence of an attack on the night of July 29. On June 20, 2023, a prisoner exchange released 144 Ukrainian soldiers, including 95 from Azovstal. Between May 16 and 20, approximately 2,500 defenders of Mariupol (36th Marine Brigade, Azov, National Guard, Police, Border Guard, Territorial Defense) evacuated from the factory. They remain in Russian custody or on occupied territories. On May 19, Deputy Commander of Azov, Svyatoslav Palamar ('Kalyna'), said, 'Thank you to the whole world and thank you to Ukraine for support. See you soon.' The siege of Azovstal lasted over a month, with continuous aerial bombardment. Commanders like Sergey Volynsky (36th Marine Brigade) and Denys Prokopenko (Azov) repeatedly called for international help to evacuate the wounded, noting that many died from gangrene due to lack of antibiotics, anesthesia, and surgical tools. Turkey offered mediation for third-country extraction. Before military personnel, civilians were evacuated, with many separated from family—such as a 4-year-old girl separated from her mother, who was sent to a Russian filtration camp. The Zaporizhzhia Children's Services reported this as the 36th case of a child arriving unaccompanied. According to the Ukrainian General Staff, holding Azovstal prevented Russia from redeploying 17 battalion tactical groups (~20,000 personnel) to other fronts. UK intelligence reported that Ukrainian defense in Mariupol significantly degraded Russian combat effectiveness. Additional locations mentioned: Vinogradnoye, Staroye Krym, Mangush near Mariupol cemetery.

Ukrainian soldiers detected and destroyed these groups through precision strikes, as shown in video footage depicting Russian positions in the buildings engulfed in flames. The operation took place on November 5, 2025.

articles.title: Pokrovsk: Ukraine’s Surprise Counteroffensive Challenges Russian Advances
articles.summary: In Pokrovsk, one of the most intense battles of the past three years of war in Ukraine, Ukrainian forces have launched a surprise counteroffensive against Russian advances after weeks of siege. According to Ukrainian media, special forces and aerial units of the military intelligence (HUR) conducted an airborne operation, with assault units infiltrating areas previously considered under Russian control. Pokrovsk is a strategically important rail and road junction for Russia, potentially enabling further advances in the Donetsk region. Ukrainian forces have made marginal gains in recent counterattacks north of Pokrovsk, effectively halting Russian momentum. Meanwhile, Russian troops continue to infiltrate Pokrovsk and areas east of Myrnohrad. Geolocated footage published on October 31 shows Ukrainian forces capturing territory in eastern Rodynske (north of Pokrovsk). Footage from October 30 indicates Ukrainian strikes on Russian positions in the northern part of Pokrovsk and eastern Rih (immediately east of Pokrovsk), following what the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) assesses as a penetration mission. A source affiliated with Ukraine’s military intelligence stated on October 29 that Russian forces are infiltrating Pokrovsk in groups of five to ten soldiers, describing the area as a contested 'gray zone'. The Russian Ministry of Defense reported that elements of the 2nd Combined Arms Army are advancing within Pokrovsk, including near the central railway station, and that the 5th Motorized Rifle Brigade is advancing toward Myrnohrad.

articles.title: Putin Believes Donetsk Oblast Will Eventually Fall Under Russian Control, U.S. Official Says
articles.summary: According to a senior U.S. official speaking to CBS News, Russian dictator Vladimir Putin believes that Donetsk Oblast will eventually come under Russian control, regardless of whether through negotiations or military advances. The official noted that U.S. talks in Geneva were based on the assumption that Putin sees the capture of Donetsk as inevitable. While the official declined to assess whether Ukraine could lose the war in the east, they acknowledged that the current military dynamics 'indicate that Russia may capture Donetsk Oblast.' As of November 25, 2025, much of the city of Pokrovsk in Donetsk Oblast is under Russian control, with Ukrainian forces holding only the northern part. The southern part of the city, south of the railway line, is in Russian hands, according to the Ukrainian online outlet 'Ukrainska Pravda.' The publication stated that the General Staff's map of the Pokrovsk front is at least one month behind reality. Failed attempts to recapture Pokrovsk were due to the overwhelming number of Russian troops in the city. Although Ukrainian counterattacks in the nearby settlement of Rodynske were initially successful, the area was quickly reoccupied. A recent claim by the 7th Air Assault Corps about clearing the center of Pokrovsk does not reflect the actual situation. Russia’s success in capturing Pokrovsk is attributed largely to drone warfare. In August, Russian forces achieved air dominance over Pokrovsk, enabling the operation of one of their most effective drone units, 'Rubikon,' which disrupted Ukrainian logistics and troop rotations, as reported by 'Ukrainska Pravda.'

articles.title: Battle for Pokrovsk and Kup'yansk: Russia's Strategy and Ukraine's Defense Amid Escalating Frontline Struggles
articles.summary: The article analyzes the ongoing military situation around Pokrovsk and Kup'yansk in Ukraine's Donets'k Oblast, focusing on Russian strategic objectives and Ukrainian defensive efforts. As of November 16, 2025, intense and complex battles continue in both cities, with Russian forces attempting to encircle Pokrovsk through multi-directional infiltration—particularly from the south, southwest, and north via Krasnyi Lyman and Rodynske. Ukrainian forces report that between 300 and 500 Russian soldiers are present in Pokrovsk, with fighting concentrated in a fragmented control zone: southern and southwestern areas under Russian control, central areas as a contested 'gray zone,' and northern areas held by Ukrainian forces. The Russian goal is to link up forces from the 2nd Combined Arms Army (approaching from the west) and the 51st Army (advancing from the north) near the village of Hryshyne to fully encircle the Pokrovsk agglomeration. Ukrainian forces have disrupted these plans through counterattacks, such as in Rodynske, and maintain resistance despite significant challenges. Moscow's latest deadline for capturing Pokrovsk is December 15, 2025, though some Ukrainian sources express doubt about its feasibility due to manpower shortages and communication breakdowns. In Kup'yansk, Russian forces are advancing from the north and west along the Oskil River, aiming to control the R07 highway (Kup'yansk-Chuhuiv), which is operationally critical. Ukrainian sources estimate around 70 Russian soldiers in the city, with Ukrainian forces controlling at least half of the territory. Russian forces are limited to a small northern bridgehead and rely on precarious supply lines via river crossings and pipelines. Ukrainian forces are actively targeting these logistics routes. Russian strategy in Kup'yansk aims to push Ukrainian troops from the left bank of the Oskil River, capture the Borova–Izium–Sviatohirsk–Lymanskyi corridor, and establish a flanking position for an offensive toward Slov'yans'k—mirroring 2022 tactics. A broader Russian strategic goal, according to Ukrainian military sources, is to achieve these objectives by the end of 2025, though full territorial capture is deemed unrealistic. The article notes that Ukrainian leadership, including the President, has prioritized the defense of both cities, directing resources and personal oversight to prevent encirclement and further Russian advances.

articles.title: Pokrovsk: Kyiv's Surprise Move in Dobropillia Halts Russian Advance
articles.summary: The Russian military has advanced significantly in Ukraine during October 2025, capturing 461 square kilometers of territory, primarily in the eastern Donetsk Oblast, according to data from the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) analyzed by AFP. The city of Pokrovsk in Donetsk has become a focal point of intense fighting, with Ukrainian forces working to halt Russian advances. Ukrainian forces reported stopping a Russian push north of Pokrovsk and preventing the enemy from blocking a key road connecting Pokrovsk to Rodynske. The 7th Rapid Reaction Brigade of Ukraine’s Airborne Forces stated on Facebook that 'active clearing of the northern part of Pokrovsk from occupiers is underway,' and that coordinated defense actions have halted Russian expansion in the area. On November 2, 2025, Ukrainian forces claimed to have eliminated 19 Russian soldiers in the city. Additionally, Russia captured 150 square kilometers in the Dnipropetrovsk region, west of Donetsk.
